To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel RNA-seq-assisted method for MCH class I genotyping that is more comprehensive than existing methods, because it avoids preselection of MHC locii, and that we have applied the method to a lethal, vaccination induced disease of cattle for which MHC alleles had been postualated as causal agents.

RAMHCIT allows comprehensive MHC class typing at nucleotide resolution and quantification of MCH class I expression, and that the MHC class I locus in cattle is highly diverse, but the diversity is not related to the disease phenotype.
we developed a new method for MHC genotyping and that we applied it successfully to cattle.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel, RNAseq-assisted MHC genotyping method, which can be applied to a wide range of species, including non-model species, and provides a novel approach to the investigation of MHC class II genes.
the development of a novel, RNAseq-based method for MHC typing in non-model species and its application in an immunological context.

the development of a new, comprehensive method for MHC genotyping and allele quantification, which is highly applicable for non-model species and has been demonstrated on a real-world data set from a cattle disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RAMHCIT is a highly sensitive method for MHC genotyping in cattle and other non-model species.

the RAMHCIT method is a powerful, fast, and reliable method to discover and identify MHC class I allelic diversity and to quantify MHC class I gene expression at allele level in a non-model mammalian species.
MHC class I genes are not the cause of bovine neonatal pencytopenia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RNAseq is a promising approach for MHC class II typing in non-model species and that RNAseq-assisted MHC typing is a powerful tool for genetic studies on immune diseases.

RAMHCIT enables a comprehensive and quantitative MHC class I analysis in non-model species and that this method is particularly useful for MHC class II typing, where the high variability of the MHC class II locus poses a challenge for the discovery of new alleles.

RNAseq-assisted MHC genotyping is a novel, powerful method for MHC typing in non-model species and that RAMHCIT is a useful tool for future research in immunogenetics, population genetics and biodiversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RAMHCIT can be used to discover new MHC alleles, which are not covered by current MHC typing primers.
RNAseq is an ideal technology to perform MHC class I analysis at nucleotide level and RAMHCIT is the first method that enables this.

the novel RNAseq-based method RAMHCIT is a powerful tool for comprehensive MHC class 1 genotyping in any non-model species, and that MHC class  I alleles may be causal agents for bovine neonatal pacytopenia.
